thread_title: S. flava 'solid red throat' Eastern AL
breadcrumb: S. flava 'solid red throat' Eastern AL

posts.body_html:
Here's an unusual clone that I've extensively bred with but it's been a bit of a challenge to get it to color up consistently. Why breed with a plant that is difficult to color up? Because this plant has unique genes that haven't otherwise been worked with, and those traits are useful for creating unique hybrids. The color up difficult thing can be corrected in future generations.

The shape of this clone is very different from other flavas, and the lid can get really big relative to the rest of the trap! Under optimal conditions, the throat can become solid red, but it's a bit different than extreme red throat....maybe more like flava rubricorpora solid red throat.

Anyways, thought I'd photodocument this clone for future reference, pics taken mid May 2019:

posts.body_html:
Well look what S. flava 'solid red throat' Eastern AL decided to do this year! On a side note, It probably wasn't stated very clearly, but this is one of the parents of S. moorei 'white top, red body' Eastern AL, which essentially looks like Adrian Slack but with a red body! Zero adrian slack genes in it! I'm not certain, but I'm confident the other parent was a moorei from Eastern AL, I messed up the details when making the cross years ago, so I'm not 100% positive. Ya, this thing is stunning:






Anyways, now that the offspring stole the spotlight, here's one of the "crappy" but genetically amazing parents. Never, ever underestimate the power of the OK lookers...well, this one ain't too ugly, but it's been a tough cookie to color up. pics taken 5/17/20:
